texts.facts: Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122640175/ 1 1. Present claim petition has been filed under Section 166 and 140 of M.V. Act seeking compensation in respect of injuries suffered by petitioner Upender Pandey in an accident taken place on 29/30.12.2015. It is stated that on 29.12.2015 petitioner was going to his home and on his way at Metro Site, U.P. Border, Mata Mandir, G.T. Road some persons were standing near fire. The petitioner stood there and after some time at about 3 a.m. a Man Lift crane make 10 Ton capacity, model Genie Z45, Machine serial no:Z4508-1320 (hereinafter referred as offending vehicle), which was engaged in metro work came from behind and hit the petitioner due to which petitioner suffered grievous injuries. Petitioner was taken to Yashoda Hospital by the driver of the crane and an employee of metro. Regarding the accident in question an FIR No.98/2016 was registered in PS Sahibabad under Section 279/338 IPC. It is stated that at the time of accident petitioner was 35 years old and was earning Rs.15,000/- to Rs.20,000/- per month while working as a helper in a transport company. 2. Originally claim petition was filed against four respondents. Respondent no.1 being DMRC at whose site the accident had occurred. It is stated that respondent no.2 is owner of offending crane belonging to Man Lift India Private Limited and respondent no.3 is driver of the same. Offending vehicle is stated to be insured with respondent no.4/insurance company (HDFC Ergo General Insurance). 3. During the pendency of claim petition an application under Order 1 Rule 10 CPC was moved on behalf of respondent no.1 to implead M/s GYT-TPL JV as the civil work of metro project at the DMRC site of MACT No.1710/2016 by SHAILENDER Page 2 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.05.17 16:47:07 +0530 Dilshad Garden to New Bus Adda Ghaziabad was awarded to M/s GYT- TPL JV, under an agreement. Said application was allowed vide order dated 14.12.2017 and M/s GYT-TPL JV was impleaded as respondent no.5. 4. Initially respondent no.4/insurance failed to file the WS despite giving opportunities, consequently defence was closed vide order dated 06.02.2018. Thereafter an application was moved on behalf of respondent no.4/insurance seeking permission to file WS on record. Said application was allowed vide order dated 28.09.2018 and WS of respondent no.4 was taken on record. 5. WS on behalf respondent no.1/Delhi Metro Rail Corporation Limited has been filed wherein an objection has been taken that there is no cause of action against R1 as the R1 had already awarded the contract C-87 for civil works from Dilshad Garden to New Bus Adda, Ghaziabad to M/s GYT-TPL JV (respondent no.5) and safety and security at the working site was sole responsibility of R5. Contents of claim petition have been denied in totality. 6. WS on behalf respondent no.2 and 3 has been filed wherein it is pleaded that injured himself went to the site of construction and stood there. It is admitted that injured was taken to hospital by crane driver and staff of Metro. It is denied that accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of respondent no.3. It is pleaded that petitioner was standing without any cogent reason nor he was employee of respondents. Contents of claim petition as well as liability to pay compensation have been denied. Upender Pandey vs Delhi Metro Corporation Ltd on 17 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122640175/ 2 7. In its WS respondent no.4/insurance company has taken the objection that no cause of action arose under M.V. Act against the offending crane/machine. It is pleaded that R4 is insurer of contractor's MACT No.1710/2016 SHAILENDER MALIK Page 3 MALIK Date: 2024.05.17 16:47:16 +0530 plant and machinery under the Contractor's Plant and Machinery Policy no.2224200502506602000 valid from 09.10.2015 to 15.05.2016 but the same is not applicable to provisions of M.V. Act. It is pleaded that as per Section 8 of the policy as R4 never issued any policy under the provision of Section 146 of M.V. Act and as such does not provide coverage of third party risks on public road. Contents of claim petition have been denied. 8. Respondent no.5 in its WS has taken the objection that R5 has been impleaded at a belated stage but being the contractor for Metro site where the alleged accident took place. It is stated that no cause of action arose against R5. It is pleaded that there is no contributory negligence on the part of R5 and it is petitioner himself who without any authority or right intruded into and remained at the cordoned off area at construction site at odd hours. It is pleaded that in view of Work Order dated 11.12.2015 respondent no.5 is not liable to pay any compensation to petitioner as the contractor/R2 is liable for liability arising out of site activities carried out by it. 9. On the basis of pleadings of parties following issues were framed by ld. Predecessor on 06.02.2018 : 10. Petitioner in order to substantiate his claim examined three witnesses. PW1 is Yogender Pandey, brother of the petitioner/injured, PW2 MACT No.1710/2016 by SHAILENDER Page 4 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK 11. On behalf of respondent no.1/Delhi Metro Rail Corporation Limited one witness R1W1 Piyush Goyla, Junior Engineer/Civil has been examined. Respondent no.4 examined one witness R4W1 Simarpreet Kaur, Deputy Manager (Litigation and Claims) of insurance company. On behalf of respondent no.5 one witness R5W1 Rajesh Kumar Singh, Manager Human Resources has been examined. 14 . For proving the rash and negligent driving of offending MACT No.1710/2016 SHAILENDER Page 5 SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.05.17 16:47:31 +0530 vehicle PW2 petitioner/injured has deposed that on 29.12.2015 he was proceeding towards his house, while on the way at Metro site of UP Border, Mata Mandir Marg, GT Road some persons were standing as there was some fire at that place. PW2 says that he stood there for some time. At about 3.00 a.m. PW2 says that a Man Lift Crane, engaged in Metro work came from behind and hit him, due to which he fell down and suffered grievous injuries. PW2 says that driver of the crane and other employee of Metro toom him to Yashoda Hospital, Kaushambi. PW2 also referred to the registration of FIR No.0098/2016 at PS Sahibabad UP on 19.01.2016 u/s 279/338 IPC. 15. Nothing substantive came int eh cross examination of PW2 rather witness reiterated in hhis cross examination that whiile he saw some persons standing near hte fire, he stood for the time being and in the meantime the crane hit him from behind. PW2 in cross examination by counsel for insurance specifically denied the suggestion of accident having taken place due to his negligence or carelessness. As such nothing came in the cross examination of PW2 to disbelieve the version regrding the accident as well as the factum of rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle/crane which hit the petitioner from behind. Evidence of PW2 gets corroboration from the factum of criminal case registered against respondent no.3/driver of the offending vehicle. To prove this fact petitioner has proved medical bills as Ex.PW2/2 (colly.) totaling of which comes out to be Rs.9,273/-.
texts.arguments: Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Others (2009) 13 SC 530, Parmeshwari v. Amirchand & Others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 & Mangla Ram v. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. & Others 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303. The scope of compensation in injury cases has been considered by Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Mr. R.D. Hattangadi v. M/s Pest Control (India) Pvt. Ltd., 1995 AIR 755. The relevant extract is as under: "Broadly speaking while fixing an amount of compensation payable to a victim of an accident, the damages have to be assessed separately as pecuniary damages and special damages. Pecuniary damages are those which the victim has actually incurred Upender Pandey vs Delhi Metro Corporation Ltd on 17 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122640175/ 4 and which is capable of being calculated in terms of money-, whereas non-pecuniary damages are those which are incapable of being assessed by arithmetical calculations. In order to appreciate two concepts pecuniary damages may, include expenses incurred by the claimant: (i) medical attendance; (ii) loss of earning of profit upto the date of trial; (iii) other material loss. So far non- pecuniary damages are concerned , they may include (i) damages for mental and physical shock, pain suffering, already suffered or likely to be suffered in future; (ii) damages to compensate for the loss of amenities of life which may include a variety of matters i.e. on account of injury the claimant may not be able to walk, run or sit; (iii) damages for the loss of expectation of life, i.e. on account of injury the normal longevity of the person concerned is shortened; (iv) inconvenience, discomfort, disappointment, hardship, frustration and mental stress in life." 17. Further, in Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & another (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India laid down general principles for computation of compensation in injury cases. The relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced as under: 4. The provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, MACT No.1710/2016 by SHAILENDER SHAILENDER MALIK Page 7 MALIK Date: 2024.05.17 16:47:52 +0530 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. 5. The heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary Damages (special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: Upender Pandey vs Delhi Metro Corporation Ltd on 17 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122640175/ 5 (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment. (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-Pecuniary Damages (general damages) (iv) Damages to pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). MACT No.1710/2016 Digitally signed by Page 8 SHAILENDER SHAILENDER MALIK MALIK Date: 2024.05.17 16:47:58 +0530 It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii), (b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. 18. In case of Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 SCC 343, Hon'ble Supreme Court of India determined the broad criteria for assessment of permanent disability for ascertaining the purpose of future loss of earning and also laid down step by step procedure for assessment of disability and for ascertainment to the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity. Relevant paras of the judgment are reproduced as under:- MACT No.1710/2016 SHAILENDER Page 10 MALIK Date: 2024.05.17 16:48:13 +0530 "9. 26. It is argued by the counsel for the petitioner that due to accidental injuries and permanent disability, petitioner lost his livelihood as he is unable to do his work properly. Dr.Sushil Kamal (PW3) who proved medical disability certificate of petitioner/injured during cross examination has stated that petitioner will not be able to sit cross legged, squat or kneel down. He also stated that petitioner will face difficulty in walking on uneven surfaces and surfaces which bear a slope as well as difficulty in climbing stairs and to lift weight. 27. In Raj Kumar vs. Ajay Kumar (supra) Hon'ble Apex Court in para 11 and 12 has observed that Tribunal should not be a silent spectator when medical evidence is tendered regarding injuries. As such multiplier to be applied in the present case would be 15 as applicable to age group between 36-40 years, would be applicable as per settled principle laid down in case of Sarla Verma v. DTC (2009) 6 SCC 121. Moreover, the law has been well settled by the decisions of Supreme Court in the cases of Sandeep Khanuja (supra) and Erudhaya Priya vs. State Express Transport Corporation Ltd., 2020 SCC OnLine SC 601, that while applying the multiplier method, future prospects on advancement in life and career are also to be taken into consideration. While discussing the criteria to ascertain the compensation for pain and sufferings by victim of vehicular accident, observations of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in Satya Narain v. Jai Kishan, FAO No: 709/02, date of decision: 02.02.2007 can be considered: It is argued by the counsel for the insurance that the crane from which accident had Upender Pandey vs Delhi Metro Corporation Ltd on 17 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122640175/ 12 occurred, cannot be considered to be a motor vehicle as defined under M.V. Act and therefore liability cannot be fixed upon the insurance company. Furthermore Sh.Shrey Mehta, ld. counsel for insurance argued that liability of insurance would not be invoked in view of clause (h) of Exception of terms and policy as it was stipulated that loss or damage while the crane is in transit MACT No.1710/2016 by SHAILENDER SHAILENDER MALIK Page 18 MALIK Date: 2024.05.17 16:49:10 +0530 from location to another would be payable by the contractor's plant and machinery and would not cover with insurance risk. 41. Counsel for the petitioner on the other hand submitted that such argument of non coverage from the terms and policy is completely misplaced when there is a specific term of insurance company terms and conditions in the shape of third party liability and it is written in that terms and conditions that in respect of payment of additional premium as per the schedule, insurance company is liable against legal liability for fatal/non fatal injury to any person other than insured or own employee. 42. Having considered the submissions this Tribunal has already concluded that accident occurred due to rash and negligence of respondent no.3/driver, it impliedly means that the crane by which accident had occurred is to be considered to be a motor vehicle under the M.V. Act.
